1.5 How the Python image comparison works

The comparator requires a DNGVersion tag in each first page and traverses main and subordinate TIFF pages. It classifies primary raw pages using subfile type zero and its supported photometric codes; other pages go into the auxiliary group. It compares corresponding pages in their traversal order. Different page counts remain unverified instead of being guessed into correspondence.

For each page it validates the declared strip/tile ranges against the physical file length and reads every payload block. SHA-256 includes each block length before its bytes, so block boundaries are part of the encoded comparison. A matching payload digest is accepted on the fast path only with the selected encoding signature, including byte order and the implemented interpretation parameters.

If that path does not match, tifffile and imagecodecs decode the two pages. Shapes and complete arrays must compare equal; NaNs compare equal for this purpose. A changed decoded array is different. A missing decoder, malformed page or decode error is unverified, with its actual error retained. Differing compressed bytes alone are not classified as a pixel difference.

Here, raw samples mean the stored sensor or linear samples, including the sample margins, before rendering. Crop, white balance, orientation, DNG opcodes, profiles and develop instructions are not applied. Equal samples are therefore compatible with different appearance in Lightroom. The comparison is not an Adobe SDK validation, a demosaicing test, or proof that an identical damaged pair is healthy. OriginalRawFileData, which can contain an embedded original source file, is excluded from image payload and ExifTool comparisons; use whole-file preservation when that content must be retained.
